messages:
Ada: heads up — started a long-context run against canary model and saw a tail-latency ripple + steady KV memory growth over ~20m of sustained requests. evict/sec spikes at the same time.
Ben: do you have the evict counts/logs? any recent kernel-selection or batching changes in the canary?
Ada: yes attaching a tiny log excerpt:
```
evict_count=3125 paging_in=1216 paging_out=3089 kv_pages_prefetched=21456 kv_reuse_hits=0.03
mem_rss: 18.3GB -> 23.9GB over 20m
tail_p99_latency_ms: 240->780
```
Carla: hmm kv_pages_prefetched is huge. we shipped a more aggressive batching/prefetch heuristic in 9f3ab12 to reduce per-token latency for small-context traffic — might be overfetching for long contexts.
Dan: that commit did change kernel selection heuristics too (switch to explicit memcopy path + prefetch trigger when batch.window_tokens > 64). I suspected it could increase background IO/memory churn.
Ada: ran perf sampling — flame showed a lot of cycles in `memmove` called from prefetch path and some stalls in pager thread. snippet: `samples: 48% memmove, 12% spin_on_reclaim, 8% scheduler`.
Ela: can you repro with a minimal config? if so we should try toggling kv.prefetch_window and evict_policy to see delta.
Ada: repro steps I used (quick):
```
# launcher flags
--runtime.kv.prefetch_window=256
--runtime.kv.evict_policy=lru
--batching.max_prefetch_bytes=32MB
# curl workload: 1 long-context stream per shard, ~2500 tokens/sec sustained
```
Ben: quick mitigation idea: set `kv.prefetch_window=0` or `batching.max_prefetch_bytes=4MB` in canary. I rolled that to one host and p99 dropped from 780ms -> 210ms within 3m. evict/sec also halved.
Carla: good short term. but switching to FIFO for eviction might also reduce churn because LRU keeps resurrecting pages via prefetch-positive feedback. downside: FIFO can reduce reuse for real hot keys. need correctness check.
Dan: correctness note — FIFO interacts badly with concurrent reuse when we rely on LRU semantics in the reuse sampler. I saw a unit-test fail earlier if we blindly flip policy: `kv_reuse_order_test` expects LRU ordering.
Ada: captured a small failing trace from a test that reproduces the race — posting below. it's tiny and deterministic under stress harness.
```
[TRACE] streamA: insert keyX seq=120
[TRACE] streamB: prefetch keyX seq=121
[TRACE] evict: removed keyX (fifo)
[TRACE] streamA: expect reuse hit but got miss -> consistency assertion
```
Ela: ok we should do 2-step: 1) immediate canary tweak to reduce prefetch window, 2) run a short FIFO experiment behind a flag but with extra correctness checks and an invariant test that asserts reuse semantics. schedule on-call to monitor.
Ben: I'll open an issue with repro steps, bench numbers, and the quick rollback patch. canary id: canary/rv-4411.
Carla: also add a metric for `kv.prefetch_evicted_fraction` so we can see what fraction of prefetched pages are evicted before use. that will help tune the heuristic instead of flipping policy.
Ada: +1. current sample: prefetched=21456 used=594 -> 97% of prefetched pages were evicted unused. no wonder memory churn.
deploy-bot: rollback applied to canary/rv-4411: runtime.kv.prefetch_window=32MB -> 4MB. monitor window open for 30m. :white_check_mark:
Ada: thanks, will keep watching and post a short postmortem with perf profiles once we stabilize.
Carla: assign to eng/runtime for a followup: refine prefetch heuristic to consider long-context signals (active_stream_length, reuse_rate) before aggressive prefetch.
